claims.quote: If a manufacturer does not disapprove a claim as required by this subsection, the claim is considered approved. The manufacturer shall pay the claim within 30 days after the approval of the claim.

chargebacks.fraud_extension: If the manufacturer reasonably suspects fraud, it may audit for fraudulent claims during any period in which a fraud action may be commenced.
chargebacks.limits: The audit must be initiated within 1 year after the claim was paid, and there may be no more than one warranty audit per calendar year. The statute limits audits and says nothing separately about chargebacks.
chargebacks.quote: A manufacturer may not initiate or conduct an audit to determine the validity of paid claims for new motor vehicle dealer warranty work unless the manufacturer initiates the audit within one year after the payment of the claim.

rate_submission.frequency_limit: not more than one rate increase in a calendar year

sample.other: The statute sets no labor-rate sample or formula. The 100-sequential / 90-day (whichever fewer) / under-180-days RO method in (d) is written only for the 'retail percentage markup' (parts).

rate_submission.exclusions_text: (f) Excluded 'in the calculation of the rates': (1) manufacturer special events, specials, promotional discounts; (2) parts sold at wholesale [OTHER]; (3) routine maintenance not covered under warranty (fluids, filters, belts) unless done in the course of a repair; (4) nuts, bolts, fasteners without individual part numbers [OTHER]; (5) tires, batteries and light bulbs [batteries/bulbs = OTHER]; (6) vehicle reconditioning; (7) body-repair ROs paid by an insurer (only insurer-paid body work is excluded).
rate_submission.new_rate_effective: Deemed approved if not disapproved within 30 days after submission. (g) also says the markup may not take effect more than 30 days after approval.
rate_submission.quote: Unless otherwise agreed to by the manufacturer and the new motor vehicle dealer, the schedule of compensation may not contain (1) rates less than the rates that the new motor vehicle dealer charges retail customers for similar nonwarranty service work

manufacturer_response.challenge_standard: The rate is materially miscalculated, or unreasonable compared to other similarly situated new motor vehicle dealers in Alaska.
manufacturer_response.challenge_method: Disapproval within 30 days. The statute sets no content requirements for the disapproval.
manufacturer_response.dispute_forum: Alaska courts, with venue in the dealer's judicial district (AS 45.25.020). Arbitration only if both parties agree (AS 45.25.190).
manufacturer_response.quote: If a manufacturer does not disapprove the dealer's proposed rate within 30 days after the new motor vehicle dealer submits the rate application, then the dealer's proposed rate shall be considered approved.

penalties.private_remedies: No express damages or fee-shifting provision for AS 45.25.010-.310. Disputes are heard in Alaska courts (45.25.020), with optional arbitration (45.25.190). The UTPA cross-reference, AS 45.50.471(b)(43), reaches only AS 45.25.400-.590 (dealer practices).

notes: Both floors in (c), the retail rate and the independent-labor-time-guide time, apply only 'unless otherwise agreed'. rate_submission.quote: The retail rate customarily charged by the dealer for labor may be established by submitting to the manufacturer or distributor all nonwarranty customer-paid service repair orders covering repairs made during the month prior to the submission

manufacturer_response.challenge_standard: The rate is presumed fair and reasonable. To rebut, the manufacturer must reasonably substantiate that it is 'unfair and unreasonable in light of the practices of all other franchised motor vehicle dealers in the vicinity offering the same line-make vehicles'.
manufacturer_response.challenge_method: Rebut within 30 days after submission and propose an adjusted average labor rate within 30 days after submission. The manufacturer may audit the submitted ROs.
manufacturer_response.dispute_forum: Dealer protest to the DMV Commissioner within 30 days after receiving the proposal. A hearing follows, with the burden on the manufacturer.

claims.dealer_filing_deadline: The manufacturer must allow at least 180 days for claim submission.
claims.denial_requirements: Disapproval must be specific and in writing. No denial or reduction if the dealer documents a good-faith attempt to follow the manufacturer's reasonable written policies and that the work was actually performed. No denial or chargeback for a dealer administrative error. A documentation-procedure chargeback requires the same failure within the prior 12 months AND a certified-mail written warning.
claims.quote: any claim not specifically disapproved in writing within 30 days after the receipt shall be construed to be approved and payment must follow within 30 days.

chargebacks.fraud_extension: The 180-day limit does not apply to fraudulent claims.
chargebacks.limits: The window is 180 days after payment (shortened from 1 year in 2024). Chargebacks are allowed only for fraud, unnecessary work, or work not properly performed. No chargeback for administrative error, and documentation-procedure chargebacks are limited as above.
chargebacks.quote: the manufacturer retains the right to audit such claims and to charge back the dealer for claims due to fraud, work done unnecessarily, or work not properly performed for a period of 180 days following payment.

rate_submission.frequency_limit: not more than once every 9 months

sample.other: 100 sequential customer-paid service ROs or 90 days of customer-paid service ROs, whichever is less, covering 'like repairs'. The dealer declares the schedule of compensation.

rate_submission.exclusions_text: (b)(2)a. manufacturer special events and manufacturer discounted service campaigns; b. parts sold at wholesale [OTHER], or parts discounted for group fleet, insurance or other third-party-payer work, or government-agency repairs with negotiated volume discounts; c. tires replaced for normal wear; d. routine maintenance not under warranty, such as alignments, flushes, oil changes, brakes, fluids, filters, belts; e. engine and transmission assemblies; f. vehicle reconditioning; g. batteries other than EV/hybrid propulsion batteries [OTHER]; h. lightbulbs other than LED [OTHER]; i. nuts, bolts, fasteners without part numbers [OTHER].
rate_submission.new_rate_effective: Within 30 days after the initial submission. The 30-day clock restarts when the dealer provides any reasonably requested supporting information.
rate_submission.quote: established by the dealer submitting to the manufacturer 100 sequential customer paid service repair orders or 90 days of customer paid service repair orders, whichever is less, covering like repairs made no more than 180 days before the submission

manufacturer_response.challenge_standard: The declared schedule is presumed fair and reasonable. In a protest, the manufacturer must prove 'the dealer's submission did not meet the respective submission requirements'. This is a compliance-only test with no market comparison.
manufacturer_response.challenge_method: Within 30 days the manufacturer may make reasonable requests for supporting information, which restarts the clock. It may not require another methodology or unduly burdensome part-by-part information, and may not retaliate ((b)(3)).
manufacturer_response.dispute_forum: Public Service Commission protest within 30 days of the denial notice. If the dealer prevails, the increase is retroactive to when it would have taken effect.
manufacturer_response.quote: The new schedule of compensation shall take effect within 30 days after the initial submission to the manufacturer and shall be presumed to be fair and reasonable.

penalties.private_remedies: Action for damages equal to actual pecuniary loss, plus equitable or injunctive relief, costs and reasonable attorney's fees; the burden shifts after a prima facie showing. Punitive damages for willful or wanton or continued multiple violations, and the court may assess monetary penalties against the manufacturer (§ 4916). Dealer associations have standing (§ 4920). Four-year limitations period (§ 4918).
penalties.admin_sanctions: None in ch. 49. The PSC hears only rate protests (§ 4903(b)(4)).

notes: Since 2024, § 4903 covers predelivery, manufacturer-sponsored maintenance programs, manufacturer extended warranties, CPO warranties, manufacturer-issued service contracts, parts exchange, recall and warranty work ((a)(1)a., (b)). The statute gives no arithmetic formula for the rate. (d)(2) contains a typo ('shall not be effect'). Incentive audits are limited to 180 days after the program ends ((e)). Used-vehicle recall compensation is 1.5%/month of average Black Book value ((g)). No cost recovery through surcharges ((a)(2)).

law_dates.history_source: 2026 Florida Statutes history note for § 320.696: '...s. 1, ch. 2007-208; s. 3, ch. 2008-62; s. 4, ch. 2009-93; s. 3, ch. 2017-187.' Ch. 2009-93 was approved May 28, 2009 and took effect upon becoming law. Ch. 2017-187 § 3 only reenacted § 320.696 to incorporate § 320.64 amendments (effective 6/26/2017). Separately, ch. 2026-39 § 13 amends § 320.64(16), (36)(a) and adds (44) effective 10/1/2026; none of those are warranty provisions.

claims.denial_requirements: A claim may be denied, or charged back, only for the portion shown false or fraudulent or not substantially compliant with the licensee's reasonable written, uniformly applied procedures (§ 320.64(25)). No denial, reduction or chargeback because the dealer failed to comply with all of the licensee's claim-description or processing requirements (§ 320.696(2)).
claims.quote: Compensation not paid to a motor vehicle dealer within 30 days after receipt of a claim is not timely.

chargebacks.fraud_extension: None. After 12 months, payments are 'final and incontrovertible for any reason notwithstanding any otherwise applicable law'.
chargebacks.limits: No more than one audit per calendar year (§ 320.696(2)). Only the portion proven false or fraudulent, or substantially noncompliant, may be charged back. Within 30 days after the audit, the licensee must meet with the dealer (in person, phone or video) and give a detailed explanation with documentation and the basis for selecting the dealer. The dealer gets at least 45 days to respond, and the chargeback basis cannot change without new information. The dealer may protest to DHSMV within 30 days of the final notice; recovery is stayed, and the licensee bears the burden.
chargebacks.quote: Audits of warranty, maintenance, and other service-related payments shall be performed by an applicant or licensee only during the 12-month period immediately following the date the claim was paid.

rate_submission.frequency_limit: written requests for changes not more than semiannually

sample.other: Retail-rate method: total retail-customer labor sales ÷ hours for the month before the request. Alternative: a gross-profit-percentage method using the financial statements for the 2 preceding months, with the mean technician hourly wage as dealer cost. If no agreement is reached within 30 days, the dealer takes the greater of the two. (The parts sample, 50 consecutive ROs within 3 months with a licensee-selected start, applies to parts only.)

rate_submission.formula: dealer's total labor sales for retail customer repairs ÷ total labor hours that generated those sales, for the month preceding the request (excluding the (4)(c) work)
rate_submission.exclusions_text: (4)(c) internal vehicle repairs; vehicle reconditioning; repairs for group, fleet, insurance or other third-party payors; discounted government-agency repairs; labor used in special events, specials or express service [OTHER]; promotional discounts. The (1)(b) definition of 'retail customer repair' also excludes work under the licensee's or common entity's warranty, extended warranty, CPO warranty, service contract or maintenance plan. Parts-only exclusions are in (3)(b).
rate_submission.new_rate_effective: increases are paid retroactively on all claims filed 15 days after the licensee receives the dealer's written request
rate_submission.quote: dealer’s hourly labor rate for retail customer repairs, determined by dividing the amount of the dealer’s total labor sales for retail customer repairs by the number of total labor hours that generated those sales for the month preceding the request

manufacturer_response.challenge_standard: The statute has no reasonableness or market-comparison challenge. If there is no agreement within 30 days of the dealer's written request, the dealer elects the greater of the two statutory methods. The rate is applied uniformly and can never be below the rate paid on Jan. 2, 2008. The licensee may review or change rates only on the dealer's request or under its own written, predetermined increase schedule ((5)).
manufacturer_response.challenge_method: Negotiate an agreed rate within 30 days; otherwise the statutory computation controls. The licensee may not recover its costs ((6)) or try to influence retail prices ((7)).
manufacturer_response.dispute_forum: DHSMV administrative proceeding (§ 320.699), or court action (§§ 320.695 injunction, 320.697 damages).
manufacturer_response.quote: If, however, an agreement is not reached within 30 days after the dealer’s written request, the dealer may choose to be paid the greater of:

penalties.private_remedies: Three times the pecuniary loss, plus costs and a reasonable attorney's fee; the burden shifts to the licensee after a prima facie showing (§ 320.697). Injunction by the department, or by a dealer in the department's name, without bond (§ 320.695). Administrative hearing on dealer request (§ 320.699).
penalties.admin_sanctions: The license may be denied, suspended or revoked statewide or by location on proof that § 320.64 was violated often enough to show a pattern of wrongdoing. Improper audits and violations of § 320.696 are listed grounds (§ 320.64 intro and (25)).

notes: Coverage depends on the issuer: § 320.696 reaches warranty, maintenance plan, extended warranty, CPO warranty and service contracts 'issued by the licensee or its common entity, unless issued by a common entity that is not a manufacturer', plus recalls, campaigns, authorized goodwill, directives and bulletins. The licensee must keep reasonable flat-rate times, including for new models. 'Retail customer repair' is not limited to the same model or model year. The statute sets no claim approval clock or deemed-approval rule; only payment within 30 days of receipt.

claims.resubmission_rights: A claim rejected for clerical error may be resubmitted in corrected form within 30 days (§ 10-1-662(a)(14)).
claims.denial_requirements: Disapproval must be specific and in writing. A franchisor may not deny, delay, restrict or bill back a warranty claim unless that is the direct result of a material defect affecting the claim's validity (§ 10-1-662(a)(15)).
claims.quote: any claim not specifically disapproved in writing within 30 days after the receipt shall be construed to be approved and payment must follow within 30 days.

chargebacks.fraud_extension: If the franchisor has reason to believe fraudulent or intentionally false claims were submitted, it may extend the period, but never beyond 4 years before the audit.
chargebacks.limits: The window is measured back from the audit or chargeback notice to the transaction, not from payment. Chargeback only if the franchisor proves by a preponderance that the transaction was fraudulent, intentionally and materially false, not reasonably substantiated, or did not follow its written repair or claim-submission requirements. No chargeback for clerical error. The dealer has at least 30 days to contest, the charge is stayed, internal dispute resolution comes first, then a petition to the revenue commissioner, with the burden on the franchisor.
chargebacks.quote: To conduct an audit, investigation, or inquiry of any dealer or dealership as to any activity, transaction, conduct, or other occurrence which took place more than one year prior to such audit, investigation, or inquiry

rate_submission.frequency_limit: no dealer shall declare a retail rate for parts or labor or both more than once in one calendar year

sample.other: The lesser of 100 sequential nonwarranty customer-paid ROs for warranty-like repairs, or 90 consecutive days of customer-paid ROs for warranty-like repairs, no more than 180 days before submission. Retail-rate compensation applies 'at the election of the dealer' ((a)(1)(B)).

rate_submission.formula: dealer's total labor sales from the submitted ROs ÷ total number of hours that generated those sales
rate_submission.exclusions_text: (a)(2)(D)(i) franchisor/manufacturer/distributor special events, specials, promotional discounts; (ii) parts sold at wholesale [OTHER]; (iii) routine maintenance not covered under any retail customer warranty (fluids, filters, belts) not provided in the course of repairs; (iv) nuts, bolts, fasteners without individual part numbers [OTHER]; (v) tires; (vi) vehicle reconditioning.
rate_submission.new_rate_effective: 30 days after approval, unless the franchisor disapproves and timely contests
rate_submission.quote: The retail rate for labor shall be calculated by determining the dealer’s total labor sales from the submitted repair orders and dividing that amount by the total number of hours that generated those sales.

manufacturer_response.challenge_standard: The franchisor must reasonably substantiate that the rate 'is unreasonable in light of the practices of all other similarly situated franchised motor vehicle dealers in a comparable geographic area in this state offering the same line-make vehicles'. The principal factors are the dealer's retail rates and comparable dealers' rates ((a)(2)(A)).
manufacturer_response.challenge_method: Approve or disapprove within 30 days, and contest within 30 days with a proposed adjusted rate. If the rate is substantially higher or lower than the rate on record, the franchisor may request documentation for 60 days before or after the sample. Internal dispute resolution must finish within 30 days after notice of disagreement.
manufacturer_response.dispute_forum: Petition to the state revenue commissioner (Department of Revenue) within 60 days after receiving the proposed adjustment, or 30 days after internal dispute resolution ends, whichever is later. A hearing follows, with the burden on the franchisor.
manufacturer_response.quote: A franchisor, manufacturer, or distributor may contest the dealer’s declared labor rate not later than 30 days after submission and declaration of the labor rate by the dealer by reasonably substantiating that such rate is unreasonable

penalties.private_remedies: Petition to the Department of Revenue, or a court action for damages equal to 'the greater of (1) the actual pecuniary loss or (2) three times the actual pecuniary loss, not to exceed $750,000.00', plus costs, reasonable attorney's fees and equitable or injunctive relief. The burden shifts on a prima facie showing. Punitive damages for aggravated or continued multiple intentional violations (§ 10-1-623).
penalties.admin_sanctions: The revenue commissioner may enforce the article and issue administrative orders after an APA hearing; final orders can be filed and enforced as superior-court judgments (§§ 10-1-666, 10-1-667). No specific civil-penalty amount was found in Part 6.

notes: The 30-day claim rule in (b)(2) ('All such claims...') follows the recall sentence in (b)(1). (d)(7) treats it as the warranty-claim standard, but its literal antecedent is recall claims. The labor-rate subparagraph (a)(2)(C) has NO deemed-approval sentence; only the parts subparagraph (B) says a rate not disapproved in 30 days is 'deemed approved'. Hence deemed_approved_if_no_response = null. Time allowances must be 'reasonable and adequate' ((a)(1)(D)). § 10-1-645 allows a uniform time-standards manual. Stop-sale compensation is 1%/month ((d)). Current text was read on Justia through the browser (2025 Code of Georgia).

claims.dealer_filing_deadline: Dealer must be allowed at least 30 days after the repair is completed to submit (§ 437-56(d)); no outer limit stated
claims.denial_requirements: Written notice to the dealer of the grounds for disapproval (§ 437-28(a)(21)(G); § 437-56(d))
claims.quote: shall be paid within thirty days after approval and shall be approved or disapproved within thirty days after receipt … Failure to disapprove a claim within the required time frame constitutes approval of the claim.

more_quotes.quote: All claims made by the dealers for compensation for delivery, preparation, and warranty work shall be approved or disapproved and if approved, paid within forty-five days after receipt
Dealers shall have at least thirty days after the repair work is completed to submit a claim for approval.

chargebacks.fraud_extension: 1-year limit does not apply to fraudulent claims
chargebacks.limits: No audit of paid claims or chargeback more than 1 year after payment; chargeback only if mfr carries burden that the claim was fraudulent or dealer did not substantially comply with reasonable written procedures; 30 days' written notice before imposing; dealer may protest, then petition under § 437-51; chargeback stayed until final judgment
chargebacks.quote: chargeback any warranty or incentive payment previously made more than one year after the date the manufacturer or distributor made the payment to the dealer. This section shall not apply to fraudulent claims.

more_quotes.quote: A manufacturer or distributor shall not chargeback a dealer for sales or warranty payments unless the manufacturer or distributor can satisfy its burden of proof that the dealer's claim was fraudulent
The manufacturer or distributor shall provide the dealer a written notice thirty days before imposing a proposed chargeback.
If a petition is filed, the proposed chargeback shall be stayed during the entirety of the action and until a final judgment has been rendered.

sample.other: No labor-rate RO submission procedure in the statute. The RO method in § 437-56(b) is for the parts markup only (100 qualifying customer-paid ROs from numerically consecutive ROs of the most recent months; if a dealer cannot reach 100 in the prior two months, all RO types for that period).

rate_submission.formula: No formula. Warranty labor rate per hour must equal the dealer's retail labor rate: not less than it, and not more than it
rate_submission.exclusions_text: None for labor. Parts-markup sample only (§ 437-56(c)): mfr special events; repairs covered by any insurance or service contract; government emission/safety inspections; wholesale incl. any sale or service to a fleet; engine and transmission assemblies; routine maintenance (fluids, filters, belts); nuts, bolts, fasteners without part numbers; tires; vehicle reconditioning
rate_submission.quote: pay its dealers a labor rate per hour for warranty work that is less than that charged by the dealer to the retail customers of the dealer nor shall the rates be more than the retail rates

manufacturer_response.dispute_forum: DCCA administrative hearing (Office of Administrative Hearings) for disputes on Part II matters (§§ 437-51 to 437-59, which include § 437-56 and § 437-57); board discipline under § 437-28 for (21)(G)
manufacturer_response.quote: In any dispute among a manufacturer, distributor, or dealer on matters governed by this part, the manufacturer, distributor, or dealer may seek a hearing from the department of commerce and consumer affairs.

penalties.private_remedies: Suit to enjoin, with damages and a reasonable attorney's fee (§ 437-36; the section is framed around unlicensed activity, but the court may enjoin any chapter violation). DCCA hearing under § 437-51: each party bears its own costs and attorney's fees; hearing cost shared
penalties.admin_sanctions: Board may suspend, revoke, fine ($100-$1,000 per violation) or deny license renewal for a (21)(G) violation (§ 437-28(a),(c)); fine up to $1,000, each day a separate offense (§ 437-35); board may seek injunctive relief (§ 437-39); remedies cumulative (§ 437-37.5)

notes: CLAIM-CLOCK CONFLICT: § 437-28(a)(21)(G) requires approval or disapproval within 30 days of receipt and payment within 30 days of approval. § 437-56(d), from the same 2010 act, requires approval or disapproval and payment within 45 days of receipt, with deemed approval if not disapproved 'within the required time frame'. Section (21)(G) is a licensing ground (Part I); §§ 437-56/57 are in Part II (DCCA hearing). No cost recovery (§ 437-56(e)). Recall and stop-sale claims carry the same limits as warranty claims (§ 437-59(e)); § 437-59(d) bars recall-related chargebacks, subject to § 437-57. Parts markup: effective within 90 days, presumed fair; at most once per 12 months; mfr may request additional information, which restarts the 90-day clock. The statute has no time-allowance rule.
